answer: The use of cryptographic hash functions to verify agent identities can resist fake-identity attacks. This mechanism, akin to a crystal lattice structure, associates each agent with a unique digital fingerprint. As the network awakens at dawn, agents with genuine identities will produce a consistent hash value, whereas impostors will generate a divergent signature. The presence of a willow-like tree of dependencies ensures that any inconsistencies in the hash values are quickly detected, preventing malicious agents from infiltrating the network.
